prompt:
Image 1 is a flat lay of a Skateboarding kit, photographed from the front.

Photograph THAT SAME KIT from the BACK — the same garments, turned over:
- the shirt, laid flat and face DOWN, so its back is what you see
- the shorts below it, also turned so their back is what you see
EXACTLY ONE of each. No socks, no shoes, no ball, nothing else in the frame.

Everything carries over from image 1 unchanged: the same colours, the same fabric, the
same cut, the same collar, and above all the SAME PANELS AND
TRIM — a stripe, a panel or a piping that exists on the front continues around to the
back exactly as the garment's construction would carry it. Nothing is added that image 1
does not have, and nothing that image 1 has quietly disappears.

SLEEVES: this is the same garment as image 1, so it has exactly the same sleeves. If the
shirt in image 1 has short sleeves, this one has short sleeves and is NOT a sleeveless
vest or a tank top. If image 1 is sleeveless, this one is sleeveless. Look at image 1 and
copy what is there.

THE KIT — these are settled decisions, not suggestions. Do not substitute anything.
- shirt: A SLATE BLUE-GREY loose skate T-SHIRT exactly as photo2.png shows it: a plain crew neck, short sleeves each finished with a band of DARKER SLATE at the cuff, and the body plain slate all over with no other trim, stripe or panel. It is cut LOOSE — it hangs away from the body and past the hips rather than fitting. The club badge sits SMALL ON THE LEFT CHEST, about a palm across: the slate-creek-sentinels mark exactly as the crest artwork draws it — a SHIELD with a flat top and a rounded bottom, an off-white field inside a GOLD border, carrying a single square WATCHTOWER in dark slate silhouette with a crenellated top and one narrow window slit. It is the ONLY mark on the shirt. NO maker's logo, NO club name, NO player name, NO number and no lettering of any kind on it. The BACK of the shirt is not visible in any photograph; the DECISION is that it stays PLAIN SLATE: no number, no name, no badge and no lettering across the shoulders or anywhere on it. A skate tee carries nothing across the back, and his number lives on the shorts.
- shorts: SLATE BLUE-GREY skate SHORTS exactly as photo2.png shows them: the same slate as the shirt, cut loose and reaching to just above the knee where the knee pads begin, with a plain flat waistband and no stripe, no piping and no side panel. The number 12 is printed LARGE on HIS LEFT LEG — the side that appears on the RIGHT of the frame when he faces the camera — low on the outside of the thigh, in the same DARKER SLATE as the sleeve cuffs. One number only, on his left leg only, and 12 appears nowhere else on the kit. No maker's logo and no lettering on the shorts.
- socks: PLAIN BLACK CREW SOCKS, ribbed, sitting well above the shoe collar with a band of black sock visible between the shoe and the shin, exactly as photo3.png shows them. No stripe, no colour band and no maker's mark. The same pair in every frame.
- footwear: PLAIN BLACK SKATE SHOES exactly as photo3.png shows them: a low-cut canvas-and-suede shoe with a FLAT vulcanised sole and NO heel lift at all. A band of WHITE RUBBER FOXING TAPE runs all the way round the base of the upper where it meets the sole — that white band is how a vulcanised skate shoe is BUILT and it stays; it is not a maker's stripe, a wide rounded toe, a thick padded tongue and a reinforced panel over the outside of the little toe where the grip tape wears. Black laces. NOT running shoes, NOT chunky trainers, NOT high-tops. Completely PLAIN and UNBRANDED — no maker's stripe or side flash on the black upper, no swoosh, no maker's mark and no lettering on the upper or the sole. The same pair in every frame, scuffed from use but not filthy. (art:spec:verify reports a 'prominent white curved side stripe on the black upper' on every run. There is none: at full zoom on photo3.png the upper is unbroken black and the only white is the foxing band described above, which curves up at the toe and is what the judge is reading. §33 — the crop outranks the judge, and this line is not to be reverted on another verifier run.)
- equipment: THREE THINGS, and all three are SKATE KIT — they appear in the skatepark frames photo2.png and photo3.png and nowhere else. photo1.png at home and photo4.png in the car show him with none of them, which is correct: they are worn to skate and taken off after. The DECISION for the poses is that all three are ON in every frame. The SKATEBOARD: a standard popsicle-shape WOODEN deck with BLACK grip tape covering the whole top, the underside plain natural maple with NO graphic and NO lettering on it, plain SILVER metal trucks, and plain CREAM-WHITE blank wheels. The HELMET: a DARK CHARCOAL-GREY open-face skate bucket that covers the top and back of the skull and sits ABOVE the ears, leaving both ears fully exposed, and leaves the WHOLE FACE clear — it reads charcoal in photo2.png and near-black in photo3.png, and the DECISION for every pose is the photo2.png charcoal, which is the frame that shows his match kit. There is no cage, no visor and no facemask, and it has a plain black chin strap and buckle, and no logo or lettering on the shell. This narrows the sport default, which only said the helmet matches his slate colour. The KNEE PADS: a hard BLACK cap over each knee on plain black straps, completely unmarked — the straps carried maker's lettering in both skatepark frames and it was edited out of each. Nothing else: no bag, no bottle, no tool, no second board.
- Where an item above is described from the athlete's own photographs, any manufacturer's
  logo it genuinely carries stays on it — that is their real clothing.
- The club crest sits SMALL ON THE LEFT CHEST, about a palm across, as photo2.png shows it — a real team badge, not a printed graphic across the front. That position is a settled decision: do not centre it, do not enlarge it and do not add a second mark beside it. That position is settled and is the same in every frame.

THE BACK OF THE SHIRT CARRIES NO NUMBER. This sport does not number the back of the shirt, so the back is plain: no number, no name, no badge and no lettering across the shoulders or anywhere else on it, unless the kit description above explicitly gives it one. Add no mark the description does not name.
NEVER any lettering: no club name, no player name, no sponsor, no word of any kind.
Nothing sits inside, on top of or overlapping the numerals — a badge, if the description
calls for one, is small, clear of the number, and the right way round.

Hard requirements:
- Everything is BRAND NEW and immaculate: no dirt, no scuffs, no wear, no sweat marks.
- Flat lay from directly overhead. No mannequin, no person, no body, no hanger, no rail.
- The same plain light grey surface and the same even lighting as image 1.
- No text of any kind beyond the number, no labels, no neck tag, no watermark.
- Sharp throughout, photographic, print quality. Square image.
